releases.body:
**A session's first prompt no longer freezes a shared host while it reads what changed in memory ([#10728](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10728)).** A session resumed a few hours after its last turn read the memory commits since then with one `git diff-tree` process per commit, all started at once. On a busy memory repository that was thousands of processes, and starting them blocked every session on the same host for 28 s with one session and 142 s with seven, while the finished ones piled up unreaped. The range is now read with one `git log`; the same notices come out, the longest block with seven sessions fell to 16 s, and the host's memory footprint during prompts fell from a median of 1,258 MB to 813 MB. ([#10726](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10726))

**Prompts stop freezing a shared host after every memory commit ([#10731](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10731)).** Recall skips memory notes the conversation already mentions, and it rechecked the last 200 messages against every note again after each memory commit, one note at a time. On a 7,500-note memory that took 1 to 1.7 s per session per prompt, with every session on the host waiting. Earlier answers now carry over and only notes the commit added are checked, so a recheck takes about 6 ms and the first check about 0.2 s; with seven sessions and a commit every 20 s, the host's blocked time fell from 185 s to 28 s over four and a half minutes. The notes skipped are unchanged. ([#10729](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10729))

**A relaunch's first prompt no longer recompiles your memory.** The compiled memory block and its size estimate are now saved by commit inside the memory repository's `.git` folder, never committed or synced, and read back on the next launch. On a 6,862-note memory this cut the memory step of a prompt from a median of about 178 ms to about 52 ms in the desktop app. A block built after a git read failed is used once and never saved. ([#10674](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10674))


**Anonymous usage stats now count how many accounts you have linked per provider.** `session_started` reports, per provider kind, how many accounts the engine lists for it (the same list the app's account list shows: signed-in accounts and environment-variable slots), used or not, as capped counts only, never an account name, email, token or value ([#10919](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10919)).

**The desktop app and `omo login` can share one device on a machine.** A new hidden `omo account` command (`show`, `adopt`, `token`, `export`, `forget`) lets the desktop use the same OS-keychain sign-in the CLI writes, so a machine counts as one device for memory sync and only one process ever refreshes its tokens. Secrets pass only on stdin and stdout, a refused renewal (exit 5) names the service's refusal code so the desktop can say why the sign-in ended, and a locked OS keychain is reported as its own outcome (exit 7) instead of a generic failure. On Linux, where a locked Secret Service collection reads as empty, the default collection's lock state is read over D-Bus before any secret call (libsecret would otherwise ask the keyring to show an unlock prompt), a locked collection is reported (exit 7) instead of read, and when that check cannot answer (no `gdbus` on a minimal install, no Secret Service on the bus, a slow bus) the CLI prints one notice and uses libsecret directly as before, so login never depends on `gdbus` ([#10658](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10658)).

**Memory sync can join a new device.** `omo sync enable` turns memory sync on for the device and, if the account already syncs, asks a device that already syncs to approve it. `omo sync approve` on that device answers the request. Both screens show the same 6-digit code, and the new device is admitted only after the person confirms the codes match. A

**Memory sync checks each new keyring entry without re-reading the chain before it.** The client now uses the shared receiver's incremental entry point (omo-service #600, re-vendored), and the receiver moves along with the verified chain state. Appending one entry to a 1,000-entry chain used to hand the receiver all 1,006 entries again; it now hands it one, at any chain length. What the receiver refuses is unchanged, including a replayed or lower-seq entry. ([#10694](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10694), fixes [#10655](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10655))

**The engine moves to senpi 2026.10.21-2: idle task hosts exit again, reopened sessions stop spending quota, and sessions share their prompt cache ([#10893](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10893)).** A monitor watch no longer keeps every task shard host on the machine running, so idle hosts exit as designed. Reopening an unattended session no longer spends quota on goals or background events until you send input or choose Resume. Responses prompt-cache keys follow the model, instructions and tool schemas instead of the session, so new sessions and task children with the same prefix reuse one cache. A goal waiting on a subscription limit retries at the provider's reset time instead of hammering the spent account. On Windows, input sent while a turn is running no longer gets stuck or races through the whole fallback chain. Switching a long conversation to a smaller-context model while the current one is at its limit now applies at the next message, saving an API key over an OAuth login (or the reverse) replaces the credential instead of storing one that is never used, a busy command monitor is no longer muted after 200 lines a day, and every assistant reply records its timing (time to first token and generation rate).

**OmO records when an answer says "tests pass" or "done" with nothing in the session behind it.** When a turn's final answer says tests pass, a build or typecheck is clean, a feature already exists, or the work is done, OmO checks the session for a check that passed after the last code edit, and records in the session whether the claim is backed. It starts in shadow mode: nothing is shown to you or the agent and no turn is blocked or continued, because on a week of our own sessions most flags were still false positives. Setting the `omo-senpi-claim-receipt-nudge` flag turns on a short note under a flagged answer (once per message you send) and passes the flagged claims to a gate reviewer spawned afterwards. ([#10785](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10785))

**`omo doctor --models` shows which model every task category and agent runs, and `exclude_models` keeps a model out of all of them ([#10763](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10763)).** The new doctor view prints, per category and agent, the model a spawn runs first, the retry chain in order, and each rung's source (built-in, omo.json, or the category an agent borrows) with why it does or does not run: excluded, no login, or not reached. It reads the same resolvers spawns use, and `--json` gives the same view to scripts. The new top-level `exclude_models` list (`provider/model`, a bare model id, or a `*` pattern such as `"claude-fable-*"`) is honored by category and agent chains, memory children (the session model they would inherit included), the main session's model profile, explicit task pins, and task children respawned or resumed on a recorded model, including their recorded fallback chains. Before, no setting could stop a builtin rung from running; only logging out of its provider did (#10759).

**Geeky becomes Obsessive.** The two GPT lanes' display names are now Obsessive · Normal and Obsessive · Heavy, with one-line descriptions to match and a shared caution, NOT RECOMMENDED FOR WRITING OR EVERYDAY WORK., that the session-start notice renders in bold; the `geeky-normal` and `geeky-heavy` ids

**The engine moves to senpi 2026.10.21-1: engine hosts start faster and idle far more quietly, Claude subscriptions use the native 1M context again, and desktop threads are lighter ([#10740](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10740)).** A new engine host starts about 0.1 s faster, and an idle engine host wakes 405 times per 90 s instead of 1,106. Current Claude subscription models (Fable 5, Sonnet 5, Haiku 5.5, Opus 4.7 and later) get their native 1M window back without asking for extra usage, and the Claude subscription lane runs Claude Code 2.1.306. Each desktop thread's engine supervisor starts from its own small program instead of the whole CLI, and messages and tool cards no longer keep duplicate copies (about 640 bytes per message and 2 KB per tool card). Models that models.dev marks deprecated stay available, labeled deprecated, instead of disappearing (GitHub Copilot Claude Opus 4.7, GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.4, Baseten Kimi K2 and others), and the model catalog is refreshed; some models get updated thinking levels (for example Nemotron 3 Ultra: off is now none). A message that was already delivered no longer stays listed under Steering, and with several accounts for one provider a usage limit stops failing turns once its reset has passed; a quota failure now says when it resets.

**Memory sync refuses signatures under weak Ed25519 keys.** Bun's WebCrypto accepts a signature made under a small-order public key, such as the identity key, for any message. The sync client now checks every key and signature it verifies itself, and refuses any keyring record that would bring a weak or malformed signing key into the account's keyring, including keys that appear only inside a fork-resolution's evidence. ([#10743](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10743), fixes [#10742](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10742))

**Outside full access, computer use asks before it acts on your screen as a whole.** Clicks, typing, key presses, scrolling, drags, pointer moves and holds aimed at the desktop or a display land on your real pointer and frontmost app, so they now need the same "Allow foreground computer control?" approval as foreground input; without it they fail with `ControlRequired` and nothing is sent. Input to one window in the background still needs no approval, and full access keeps working without a prompt, headless runs included. The macOS background check no longer moves your pointer back after you moved it, and a stopped session stays stopped when the desktop engine restarts. ([#10788](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10788), [#10790](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10790))

**OmO counts how often you had to repeat a standing instruction ([#10780](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10780), [#10786](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10786)).** Rules like "never filter the monitor output" now live in `system/agreements.md` with a count. When you correct the agent on something an agreement already covers, the count goes up; after the third time (`memory.agreements.needs_human_threshold`) the agent is told the rule keeps being broken and you see a notice. `/agreements` lists them and lets you add your own, acknowledge one, or drop one; the agreements you add can only be changed by you. The design is inspired by dinobot by roach (PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0); no dinobot code was used.

**The launcher deletes a legacy `~/.omo/credentials.json` left by an intermediate sign-in build.** The file held the device's private keys and account refresh material in plaintext, sometimes world-readable; upgrading removes it. Only the exact legacy shape is removed. ([#10697](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10697), [#10698](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10698))

**Report a problem from inside OmO ([#10546](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10546)).**

> 5.1.39 was never published: its release run stopped before npm, so 5.1.40 is the next release after 5.1.38.

**Onboarding saves only the facts you keep, and the TUI and the desktop share one completion flag.** The facts you accept are written through memory's own write path, and finishing onboarding in either the TUI or the desktop marks it done for both. ([#10506](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10506))

5.1.37 was tagged but its publish stopped on Linux (the release binaries outgrew their size budget), so its main packages never reached npm; everything listed for it ships in this release. ([#10566](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10566))

**Release binaries may be up to 182 MiB.** The per-platform size budget moves from 160 MiB to 182 MiB after measuring what grew: the Bun 1.4.3 runtime adds 9.5 MB to every binary and the senpi update about 1.25 MB, so linux-x64 reached 173.4 MB. Nothing was bundled by mistake. ([#10566](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10566))

5.1.36 was prepared but never published; everything listed for it ships in this release. ([#10552](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10552))

**The engine moves to senpi 2026.10.19: a hung extension handler no longer freezes a session, and queued input survives a crash.** An extension handler that never settles on a lifecycle event is named in the session after 60 s and released after 20 min, or at once on Esc or the turn deadline. Input queued with a client id is written to the session file before it is queued and delivered exactly once. The mouse wheel scrolls the transcript again while a question prompt is waiting, Alt+Q restores queued messages on WSL, and the /btw panel no longer repeats a running eval's output in the scrollback. Anthropic requests of 4096+ characters to `api.anthropic.com` are now sent gzip-compressed, as Claude Code does. ([senpi#3650](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/senpi/issues/3650), [senpi#3549](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/senpi/issues/3549), [senpi#3604](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/senpi/issues/3604), [senpi#3628](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/senpi/issues/3628), [senpi#3649](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/senpi/issues/3649), [senpi#3643](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/senpi/issues/3643), [#10552](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10552))

**Goals keep going while they make progress, and long sessions open and stay light (senpi 2026.10.18-1).** A goal no longer stops after a fixed 150 automatic continuations; it stops only after 60 in a row with no new tool effect, todo change or message from a person, and says why and that any message resumes it. Opening a very large session on a shared host no longer stalls the other sessions, a reopened session keeps only its latest compaction window in memory (four of the largest local transcripts went from 1441 MB to 216 MB of live heap), and reading a very long history over RPC pages instead of dropping the connection. A Claude subscription from `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` or an ambient Claude Code login now shows as a connected subscription, and a host daemon inherits every credential variable the engine reads. Provider accounts can be ordered, and grep starts 5 to 14 `rg` processes where it used to start 63 to 87. ([#10280](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10280), [#10509](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10509)) The engine also fixes ChatGPT browser sign-in dead-ending on "State mismatch." when another session holds the callback port ([senpi #3627](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/senpi/pull/3627)), and a compiled engine now finds the Claude Code binary shipped beside its executable instead of failing the lookup ([senpi #3640](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/senpi/pull/3640)).

**A client re-attaching to a retained session gets the full task snapshot again, and can pull it on demand.** The task RPC bridge listens for `session_resumed`, which senpi fires when the first client re-attaches to a still-open session, and re-emits the complete `omo.task.updated` snapshot instead of waiting for the next store change to alter its fingerprint; a new `omo.task.list` request answers the same payload for the parent session it names. ([#10016](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10016), [#10122](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10122))
